meta.note: High-chance exam-style MCQs + MSQs from weekly patterns

questions.stem: In the IPAT identity, which factor is best proxied by 'kg CO2 per kWh of electricity'?
questions.explanation: T (technology) captures impact intensity per unit activity; kg CO2/kWh is a classic technology factor.

questions.stem: A substance is detected in soil above natural background but causes no observed harm at that level. Course terminology would call it primarily a:
questions.explanation: Contaminant = out of place / above background; pollutant implies adverse effects or unreasonable interference.

questions.stem: For the same initial population P0, growth rate r and periods n, which model yields the largest Pn?
questions.explanation: Continuous compounding e^(rn) exceeds discrete (1+r)^n; arithmetic with X=rP0 is linear and smaller for r>0, n>1.

questions.stem: Earth Overshoot Day marks the calendar date when:

options.text: Cumulative human demand exceeds what Earth regenerates that year
All countries exhaust their national biocapacity
EPI of buildings exceeds design limits

questions.explanation: Overshoot Day = demand for the year exceeds regenerative biocapacity for that year.

questions.stem: Course global averages compare roughly _____ gha footprint/person to _____ gha biocapacity/person.
questions.explanation: Demand (~2.8 gha) exceeds supply (~1.6 gha) — global overshoot framing.

questions.stem: Energy Performance Index (EPI) for a campus is most correctly expressed as:
questions.explanation: EPI = annual energy use divided by floor area.

questions.stem: Which Supreme Court outcome is linked in Week 1 materials to a national environmental-education mandate?
questions.explanation: M.C. Mehta vs Union of India (1991) is cited for environmental education directions.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Ecological footprint and biocapacity are both expressed in global hectares.
Reason (R): Global hectares adjust land types to world-average productivity so different land uses can be compared.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; gha standardization is why EF and biocapacity share units and can be compared.

questions.stem: If India CO2 emissions grow roughly as the product of population, per-capita fossil electricity, and carbon intensity, a 2% rise in each factor implies about:
questions.explanation: For multiplicative I=P×A×T, small % changes approximately add.

questions.stem: The Brundtland (1987) definition of sustainable development emphasizes meeting present needs without:

options.text: Compromising future generations' ability to meet their needs

questions.explanation: Classic Brundtland one-liner from Our Common Future.

questions.stem: Correct chronological order for sustainability milestones is:
questions.explanation: 1987 Our Common Future → 1992 Rio → 2000 MDGs → 2015 SDGs.

questions.stem: Planetary boundaries primarily define:

options.text: A safe operating space for humanity w.r.t. Earth-system processes

questions.explanation: Rockström/Steffen framing: quantified Earth-system limits.

questions.stem: Which SDG number is most directly about climate action?
questions.explanation: SDG 13 = Climate Action; 6 water, 7 energy, 12 SCP.

questions.stem: Compared with the MDGs, the SDGs are distinctive mainly because they are:

options.text: Only eight goals for developing countries
Seventeen universal goals for all UN Member States
Legally binding emission caps for Annex I only

questions.explanation: SDGs: 17 goals, universal 2030 Agenda vs MDGs' developing-country focus.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): The three pillars of sustainability are environment, economy and society.
Reason (R): Sustainable development can be achieved by maximizing economic growth alone if technology improves.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: A is true (three pillars). R is false — all three pillars must be balanced.

questions.stem: The 'Anthropocene / Great Acceleration' narrative in the course mainly highlights:

options.text: Steep post-~1750 rises in socio-economic and Earth-system trends

questions.explanation: Coupled socio-economic and Earth-system accelerations frame why SDGs/boundaries matter.

questions.stem: Tropospheric ozone (O3) is classified as a _____ pollutant because it is _____ .

options.text: Secondary; formed by atmospheric reactions of precursors

questions.explanation: Ground-level O3 is classic secondary photochemical pollutant.

questions.stem: Which international instrument specifically targets ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs?
questions.explanation: Montreal Protocol 1987 = ODS control; do not confuse with climate treaties.

questions.stem: ESP and baghouses are primarily used to control:
questions.explanation: Electrostatic precipitators and fabric filters remove particulates (often 95–99%).

questions.stem: FGD (flue-gas desulfurization) is applied mainly to reduce emissions of:
questions.explanation: Wet limestone FGD targets sulfur dioxide from combustion.

questions.stem: 'Ambient air' in the course sense means:

options.text: Outdoor atmospheric air in its natural state that supports life

questions.explanation: Ambient = outdoor atmospheric air supporting life.

questions.stem: Criteria air pollutants are best described as:

options.text: Common pollutants for which ambient air quality standards are set

questions.explanation: Criteria = regulated common ambient pollutants with standards.

questions.stem: Stationary, mobile and area sources form a classification by:
questions.explanation: Orthogonal to primary/secondary: inventory source categories.

questions.stem: Course materials cite indoor/household air pollution mortality on the order of:
questions.explanation: ~3.2 M deaths/y (2020 cite) — major health burden.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Controlling only primary emissions of NOx and VOCs can help reduce urban ozone.
Reason (R): Ozone is emitted directly from vehicle tailpipes as a primary pollutant.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: A true (precursor control). R false — O3 is secondary, not directly emitted.

questions.stem: ASEAN Haze Agreement (2002) primarily addresses:
questions.explanation: Regional haze/transboundary smoke control among ASEAN states.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches primary vs secondary examples?

options.text: SO2, NO, CO primary; O3 and secondary PM secondary
CO2 is always a criteria ambient pollutant

questions.explanation: SO2/NO/CO/primary PM emitted; O3/secondary PM formed in air.

questions.stem: Weather differs from climate mainly in:

options.text: Weather uses only temperature; climate uses only rainfall
Weather is short-term state; climate is long-term statistics
Climate changes hourly; weather is multi-decadal
They are synonyms in IPCC usage

questions.explanation: Weather = hours–days; climate = decades+ statistics.

questions.stem: By definition, the Global Warming Potential (GWP) of CO2 is:
questions.explanation: CO2 is the reference gas: GWP = 1.

questions.stem: Ice–albedo feedback amplifies warming because ice loss tends to:

options.text: Increase albedo and reflect more sunlight
Decrease albedo so more solar energy is absorbed

questions.explanation: Darker surfaces absorb more SW → further warming.

questions.stem: Correct climate-regime timeline is:
questions.explanation: UNFCCC (Rio 1992), Kyoto 1997 (force 2005), Paris 2015 COP21.

questions.stem: Kyoto Protocol Annex I first-period target cited in course materials is about:
questions.explanation: ~5.2% below 1990 for Annex I; Doha later tightened further.

questions.stem: Mitigation vs adaptation — which statement is correct?

options.text: Mitigation only builds sea walls; adaptation cuts emissions
Mitigation reduces emissions/enhances sinks; adaptation reduces vulnerability to impacts
Adaptation replaces the need for mitigation entirely

questions.explanation: Both required: turn down the stove vs live with residual heat.

questions.stem: GHGs are described as largely transparent to _____ but absorbing _____ radiation.
questions.explanation: Transmit SW, trap outgoing IR — greenhouse mechanism.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Under the Paris Agreement, only Annex I countries submit emission pledges.
Reason (R): Paris relies on nationally determined contributions (NDCs) from parties.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: A false (all parties NDCs). R true — NDC architecture.

questions.stem: Course notes cite post-1981 warming of roughly:
questions.explanation: ~0.18 °C per decade since 1981 (course figure).

questions.stem: The IPCC's primary role emphasized in the course is to:

options.text: Operate the Green Climate Fund alone

questions.explanation: Assessment body; shared 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

questions.stem: The Betz limit states that the maximum power coefficient CP of a wind turbine is:
If wind speed doubles while ρ and A stay constant, available wind power scales by a factor of:
questions.explanation: P ∝ v³ → 2³ = 8.

questions.stem: Energy trilemma 'SEE' expands to:
questions.explanation: World Energy Council framing: Security, Equity, Environment.

questions.stem: Renewable energy is defined in the course as energy replenished at a rate:

options.text: ≥ rate of use by natural processes

questions.explanation: Replenishment ≥ use — not a claim of zero environmental impact.

questions.stem: Compared with solar PV, CSP is more naturally suited to:

options.text: Diffuse light only with no thermal storage
Concentrating heat with optional thermal storage

questions.explanation: CSP concentrates heat; thermal storage often integrated.

questions.stem: Capacity factor of a wind farm is:

options.text: Actual energy produced / energy if run at rated capacity continuously

questions.explanation: CF = actual / rated-continuous energy over the period.

questions.stem: Using ρ=1.21 kg/m³, A=π(25)² m², v=10 m/s, Betz-limited power is closest to which expression?
questions.explanation: P_wind,max = (16/27)(1/2)ρAv³ = (8/27)ρAv³.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Real commercial wind turbines often operate below the Betz CP.
Reason (R): Betz assumes an idealized actuator disk; real rotors have aerodynamic and mechanical losses, and sites have intermittency reflected in capacity factor.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; Betz is an upper bound, not a guaranteed operating CP.

questions.stem: Intermittency of solar/wind primarily motivates investment in:

options.text: Energy storage and flexible demand/grid integration

questions.explanation: Storage and flexibility bridge supply–demand mismatch.

questions.stem: Among tidal, wave and OTEC theoretical/technical potentials taught, the largest is:
questions.explanation: Rank: OTEC ≫ wave ≫ tidal (course numbers).

questions.stem: Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) mainly create value by:

options.text: Stimulating permeability in hot rock with poor natural productivity

questions.explanation: Engineer connectivity in hot dry / low-permeability rock.

questions.stem: Fast pyrolysis of biomass is characterized by roughly:

options.text: 400–600 °C with little/no O2 → bio-oil, gases, char
Excess air combustion to ash only

questions.explanation: Anaerobic thermal decomposition favoring liquids.

questions.stem: Deep-water wave power per unit crest width scales primarily with:
questions.explanation: PW ~ (ρ g² H² T)/32 — height and period dominate.

questions.stem: Hydropower efficiency e_hydro is computed as:
questions.explanation: Electric output over potential-energy rate of the flow.

questions.stem: Tidal stream resources are often screened as useful when flow speeds are about:
questions.explanation: Course threshold ~1.5–2 m/s for useful tidal stream KE.

questions.stem: Open-cycle OTEC differs from closed-cycle mainly because open-cycle:

options.text: Flash-evaporates seawater as the working vapor

questions.explanation: Open: seawater vapor; closed: low-BP secondary fluid (e.g. ammonia).

questions.stem: Geothermal heat delivery for district heating follows Q =:
questions.explanation: Sensible heat from mass flow and temperature drop.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Spring tides are typically larger than neap tides.
Reason (R): Spring tides occur when Sun–Moon–Earth are aligned so gravitational effects reinforce.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; alignment → spring; quadrature → neap.

questions.stem: Mean wave energy density E = (1/8) ρ g H² implies energy is most sensitive to errors in:
questions.explanation: E ∝ H² — height measurement errors dominate.

questions.stem: Multipurpose reservoirs for hydropower may also serve:

options.text: Only electricity with no other uses
Irrigation, flood control and water supply among other services

questions.explanation: Storage dams often multipurpose beyond power.

questions.stem: Linear urban metabolism is summarized as:
questions.explanation: One-way throughput depleting natural capital.

questions.stem: Circular economy aims to:

options.text: Keep materials in use via reuse/repair/remanufacture/recycling

questions.explanation: Close loops; design out waste.

questions.stem: Industrial symbiosis means:

options.text: Waste/by-product of one firm becomes feedstock for another

questions.explanation: Ecosystem-like material coupling in industrial clusters.

questions.stem: In the urban metabolism metaphor, catabolism corresponds mainly to:
questions.explanation: Anabolism builds stocks; catabolism yields wastes/emissions.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Closing material loops can reduce both virgin resource demand and waste emissions.
Reason (R): Circular strategies recirculate materials that would otherwise be extracted anew and discarded.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; R explains A.

questions.stem: Circular economy most directly supports which SDG theme?
questions.explanation: SCP and circularity align with SDG 12.

questions.stem: Roughly what fraction of Earth's water is freshwater (all forms)?
questions.explanation: ~97.5% salt; ~2.5% fresh (tiny usable share).

questions.stem: In NSF-WQI weighting, the single highest weight is assigned to:
questions.explanation: DO weight 0.17 (highest); fecal coliform 0.16 next.

questions.stem: Indian BOD convention often emphasized in the course is:
questions.explanation: India frequently uses BOD3 @ 27 °C.

questions.stem: Withdrawal differs from consumption because consumption is water that is:

options.text: Always returned unchanged to the source

questions.explanation: Withdrawals = consumption + returns.

questions.stem: NSF-WQI score band 90–100 is labeled:
questions.explanation: 90–100 Excellent … 0–25 Very Bad.

questions.stem: NGT was established on / by Act around:
questions.explanation: NGT Act 2010; est. 18.10.2010; natural justice; ~6-month disposal aim.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): COD is typically greater than or equal to BOD for the same sample.
Reason (R): COD measures chemically oxidizable matter, which can include substances not readily biodegradable in the BOD test.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; COD ≥ BOD usually.

questions.stem: For inland surface water discharge, course CPCB-style BOD limit cited is on the order of:
questions.explanation: Inland surface BOD ~30; sewers much higher (~350) in comparison table.

questions.stem: Correct waste hierarchy order (highest priority first) is:
questions.explanation: PRRRD: prevention first, disposal last.

questions.stem: Among the 4Rs, which sits at the top of preference?
questions.explanation: Source reduction before reuse/recycle/recover.

questions.stem: Open dumps are unacceptable mainly because they cause:

options.text: Only visual blight with no emissions
Uncontrolled leachate, CH4/VOC emissions, fires and multi-media contamination

questions.explanation: Air, water, soil and explosion risks.

questions.stem: Volatile solids (VS) as a fraction of total solids indicate:

options.text: Organic fraction lost on ignition — relevant to biodegradability

questions.explanation: VS/TS guides biological treatment suitability.

questions.stem: E-waste management in India is strongly linked to:

options.text: E-waste Rules (2011) and Extended Producer Responsibility

questions.explanation: EPR + authorized recyclers under e-waste rules.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Sanitary landfills are preferred over open dumps as disposal of last resort.
Reason (R): Engineered landfills include liners, cover, leachate and landfill-gas controls that open dumps lack.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; R explains preference within hierarchy.

questions.stem: A waste sample has 40% moisture. Total solids (TS) as wet-weight fraction is:
questions.explanation: TS = 100% − moisture = 60%.

questions.stem: For a free-field point source, doubling distance changes SPL by about:
questions.explanation: Inverse square: ΔLp ≈ −20 log(r2/r1) → −6 dB when r2=2 r1.

questions.stem: A busy highway approximated as a line source typically loses about _____ per distance doubling.
questions.explanation: Line source I ∝ 1/r → ~−3 dB per doubling.

questions.stem: Reference sound pressure P0 defining 0 dB SPL is:
questions.explanation: P0 = 20 μPa ≈ threshold of hearing.

questions.stem: Two incoherent sources each at 50 dB combine to approximately:
questions.explanation: Equal levels → +3 dB (energy sum).

questions.stem: Lp = 20 log10(Prms/P0). A tenfold increase in rms pressure raises SPL by:
Wavelength of sound λ equals:
questions.explanation: λ = c/f; period p = 1/f.

questions.stem: Approximate speed of sound relation taught is c ≈:
Occupational noise risk caution highlighted is continuous exposure around:

options.text: 0 dB forever safe regardless of duration

questions.explanation: ≥85 dB(A) 8-h occupational risk threshold (course).

questions.stem: Leq is best defined as:

options.text: Equivalent continuous level with same energy as fluctuating noise over the period
Sound power of the source in watts

questions.explanation: Energy-equivalent continuous level.

questions.stem: A-weighting is commonly used because it:

options.text: Approximates human ear frequency response for environmental/occupational limits

questions.explanation: A-network mimics ear; dominant for env/occupational limits.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): If two noise levels differ by 10 dB or more, the total is nearly equal to the louder source.
Reason (R): On the energy scale, the quieter source contributes negligibly compared with a source 10× higher in intensity (+10 dB).

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; rule of thumb for unequal combination.

questions.stem: A point source measures 70 dB at 10 m. At 40 m (same conditions) the level is nearest:
questions.explanation: Distance ×4 = two doublings → −12 dB → 58 dB.

questions.stem: BCF is defined as:
questions.explanation: BCF = tissue concentration / water concentration (L/kg).

questions.stem: Biomagnification differs from bioconcentration because biomagnification refers to:

options.text: Only uptake from water into one organism
Increase of concentration across trophic levels

questions.explanation: Bioconcentration vs water; biomagnification up the food chain.

questions.stem: USLE estimates average annual soil loss A as the product:

options.text: R × K × L × S × C × P

questions.explanation: A = R K LS C P (cover & practice are key management levers).

questions.stem: Logistic population growth approaches carrying capacity K with form:
questions.explanation: S-curve; when N≪K behaves like exponential.

questions.stem: High log Kow organics tend to:
questions.explanation: Hydrophobicity → lipid partitioning → higher BCF.

questions.stem: In ecosystems, energy flow is typically _____ while nutrients are _____.
questions.explanation: Energy one-way; mass/nutrients cycle.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Compounds with high log Kow tend to bioaccumulate strongly.
Reason (R): Such compounds are more soluble in organic phases than in water.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; hydrophobicity links Kow to accumulation (course AR pattern).

questions.stem: USLE 'unit plot' baseline dimensions cited are about:
questions.explanation: Classic USLE unit plot definition.

questions.stem: The Oleum Gas Leak case is landmark mainly for establishing:

options.text: Absolute liability for hazardous industries (no Rylands exceptions)
Public trust over Beas banks only

questions.explanation: Strict liability hardened to absolute liability — no exceptions for hazardous enterprises.

questions.stem: In Municipal Council, Ratlam vs Vardhichand, the Court held that lack of municipal funds:

options.text: Is not a valid defence against statutory public-health/sanitation duties
Transfers all liability to the Water Act alone

questions.explanation: Financial incapacity does not nullify obligatory sanitation/public nuisance duties.

questions.stem: Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) remedies included:

options.text: Coal ban/CNG shift, tannery relocation, green belt near Mathura refinery
Absolute liability for all hotels nationwide

questions.explanation: Protect 255 monuments: fuel switch, relocate tanneries, green belt.

questions.stem: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum is strongly associated with embedding:

options.text: Polluter pays / precautionary principles in Indian environmental jurisprudence

questions.explanation: Tanneries vs Palar: development cannot trump environment; polluter pays & precaution.

questions.stem: M.C. Mehta vs Kamal Nath applied which doctrine to riverbank forest lease for a motel?
questions.explanation: State as trustee of natural resources — public trust doctrine.

questions.stem: Correct sequence of major Indian statutes is:
questions.explanation: Water → Air → umbrella EPA → NGT.

questions.stem: EPA 1986 is best described as:

options.text: Umbrella central law for environmental protection and wide rule-making
A treaty identical to Montreal Protocol
Repeal of Water and Air Acts

questions.explanation: Post-Bhopal-era umbrella; parent of many Rules.

questions.stem: Act vs Rules — correct distinction:

options.text: Rules state WHAT; Acts state HOW
Acts prescribe substantive law (what); Rules detail procedures (how)

questions.explanation: Act = substance; Rules = procedure under the Act.

questions.stem: Chipko movement (Himalaya, from ~1973) is famous for:

options.text: Non-violent tree-hugging forest protection; Bahuguna marches

questions.explanation: Community forest protection; Right Livelihood Award 1987 linked in notes.

questions.stem: Appiko movement is best placed as:

options.text: Western Ghats forest protection inspired by Chipko (1982–83)

questions.explanation: Southern echo of Chipko in Karnataka Western Ghats.

questions.stem: NGT is guided by _____ and endeavors to dispose of cases within about _____.
questions.explanation: Not bound by CPC; natural justice; 6-month endeavor; benches incl. Delhi + four others.

questions.stem: Bishnoi community legacy emphasized in the course relates to:

options.text: Protecting Khejri trees / community forest ethos

questions.explanation: Sacrifice/protection legacy for Khejri precedes modern statutes.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Hazardous industries near habitation can claim Rylands-style exceptions after the Oleum case.
Reason (R): Oleum transformed the doctrine toward absolute liability without those exceptions.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: A false; R true — absolute liability eliminates traditional exceptions.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Under the public trust doctrine, the State holds certain natural resources in trust for the public.
Reason (R): M.C. Mehta vs Kamal Nath applied this doctrine to a forested Beas riverbank lease.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; Kamal Nath is the course exemplar.

questions.stem: EIA in the Week 12 framing is primarily a tool to:

options.text: Predict/evaluate impacts before project decisions and attach clearance conditions
Replace all Acts with voluntary codes

questions.explanation: Predictive, participatory assessment linked to clearances.

questions.stem: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.text: Paris — binding Annex I only like original Kyoto

questions.explanation: Montreal = ODS; Kyoto Annex I binding; Paris NDCs; UNFCCC 1992.

questions.stem: Ecological niche means primarily a species':

options.text: Functional role/position including resource use and interactions

questions.explanation: Role/position in the ecosystem.

questions.stem: If ΔL between two sources is ≥10 dB, total level ≈:
questions.explanation: Quieter contribution negligible.

questions.stem: Water Act 1974's institutional contribution includes creation/empowerment of:
questions.explanation: Boards architecture for water pollution control.

questions.stem: Air Act year (original) is:

Assertion (A): For the same r and n, exponential population growth exceeds geometric growth.
Reason (R): Continuous compounding e^(rn) is greater than discrete compounding (1+r)^n for r>0, n>0.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; e^(rn) > (1+r)^n for positive r,n — classic Week 1 trap.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Doubling the distance from a free-field point source reduces SPL by about 6 dB.
Reason (R): Intensity falls as 1/r^2, and ΔLp = −20 log10(r2/r1) equals −6 dB when r2=2 r1.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Both true; R is the quantitative explanation of the inverse-square −6 dB rule.

questions.stem: Which of the following are correctly treated as renewable natural resources?

options.text: Freshwater renewed by the hydrologic cycle

questions.explanation: Solar and wind renew continuously; freshwater renews via the hydrologic cycle. Coal is non-renewable.

questions.stem: Which combinations indicate an ecological deficit (EF = footprint, BC = biocapacity)?
questions.explanation: Deficit when EF > BC.

questions.stem: Which of the following are among the classic pillars of sustainable development?
questions.explanation: Social, environmental, and economic pillars — not militarization.

questions.stem: Which of the following are primary precursors of ground-level (tropospheric) ozone?
questions.explanation: Tropospheric O3 forms from NOx + VOCs in sunlight.

questions.stem: Which are ozone-depleting substances (ODSs) targeted in classic Montreal Protocol teaching?

options.text: Some chlorinated ODS solvents historically used

questions.explanation: CFCs/halons (and related ODSs) deplete stratospheric ozone; CO2 is mainly a GHG.

questions.stem: Which major greenhouse gases also occur naturally in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: CO2, CH4, and water vapor occur naturally; CFCs are synthetic.

questions.stem: Which are primary functions of the IPCC?

options.text: Review and synthesize peer-reviewed climate science
Run its own global climate laboratory experiments as its main role
Produce assessment reports that inform policy

questions.explanation: IPCC assesses literature and informs policy; it is not primarily an experimental lab.

questions.stem: Which factors commonly limit practical solar PV electricity yield at a site?

options.text: The Betz limit for wind turbines

questions.explanation: Betz limit applies to wind, not PV.

questions.stem: Which are recognized environmental concerns associated with wind energy?

options.text: Direct CO2 emissions during operation comparable to coal plants

questions.explanation: Operating turbines are not coal-like CO2 emitters; wildlife/noise/visuals are typical concerns.

questions.stem: Which are potential benefits of biomass pretreatment for biofuel production?

options.text: Increase surface area for enzymatic hydrolysis
Help remove or alter lignin barriers
Directly finish conversion to retail gasoline with no further steps

questions.explanation: Pretreatment prepares feedstock; it does not itself finish fuel production.

questions.stem: Which are common direct-use applications of geothermal energy?
questions.explanation: Direct-use geothermal heats buildings/processes; photosynthesis is solar-driven.

questions.stem: Which strategies align with a circular economy (not linear take-make-dispose)?
questions.explanation: Circular strategies keep materials in use.

questions.stem: Which statements about water withdrawal vs consumption are correct?

options.text: Withdrawal is water taken from a source
Consumption is the portion not returned to the source
Withdrawal and consumption are always identical
Cooling water returned to a river is largely withdrawn but not fully consumed

questions.explanation: Returned water counts as withdrawal more than consumption.

questions.stem: Which belong near the top of the ISWM hierarchy (preferred first)?

options.text: Uncontrolled open dumping as first choice

questions.explanation: Prevention, reuse, recycling beat dumping.

questions.stem: Which statements about TTS vs PTS are correct?

options.text: TTS is temporary hearing sensitivity loss that can recover
PTS always recovers fully within minutes
Repeated TTS exposures can raise risk of permanent damage

questions.explanation: TTS recovers; PTS does not.

questions.stem: Which are examples of regulating ecosystem services?
questions.explanation: Nutrient cycling is classically supporting, not regulating.

questions.stem: Which statements about ecosystem energy flow are correct?

options.text: Energy transfer between trophic levels is 100% efficient
Solar energy is the primary energy source for most ecosystems
Chemical energy in biomass moves through food webs
Energy is fully recycled like nutrients in closed loops

questions.explanation: Energy flows and dissipates; nutrients cycle.

questions.stem: Which legal ideas are strongly associated with landmark Indian environmental cases in this course?

options.text: Unlimited right to pollute if any tax is paid

questions.explanation: Oleum, Vellore, and Kamal Nath map to absolute liability, polluter pays, and public trust.

questions.stem: Which statements about the National Green Tribunal (NGT) are generally correct?

options.text: It is a specialized forum for environmental disputes
It can apply principles like polluter pays and precautionary principle
It replaces the need for any environmental statutes in India
It was created by statute to provide faster environmental adjudication

questions.explanation: NGT is a specialized statutory tribunal; it does not erase other env. laws.

questions.stem: Under a strong elevated inversion, which statements are plausible for stack emissions?

options.text: Pollutants emitted below the inversion can be trapped near the surface
Poor dispersion can worsen local air quality
Emission height relative to the inversion layer matters

questions.explanation: Inversions suppress mixing; trapping and stack height relative to the lid matter.
